plan.root_cause: The getNextActiveElement utility function does not account for disabled elements, causing keyboard navigation to move focus to disabled tabs instead of skipping to the next enabled tab.
plan.repair_strategy: Update getNextActiveElement in js/src/util/index.js to skip disabled elements when searching for the next or previous element, respecting the isCycleAllowed flag.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight and ArrowLeft navigation will now skip disabled tabs, moving focus to the next enabled tab, satisfying WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) and 2.1.1 (Keyboard).
functional_risks: Change may affect other components that use getNextActiveElement and expect to land on disabled elements (e.g., certain menu items).
If all elements in a list are disabled, the function will return the original activeElement instead of null, which could prevent focus movement.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowRight from the Account tab focuses the Billing tab and sets its aria-selected to true.
Verify that pressing ArrowLeft from the Billing tab focuses the Account tab.
Verify that ArrowRight from the Billing tab wraps to the Account tab when cycling is enabled.
Verify that dynamic enabling/disabling of tabs updates navigation behavior accordingly.
Run the existing test suite for tab, dropdown, and navbar components to ensure no regressions.
